questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the context free grammar
[latex]G=\{S \rightarrow S S, S \rightarrow a b, S \rightarrow b a, S \rightarrow \epsilon\}[/latex]

I. G is ambiguous
II. G produces all strings with equal number of a's and b's
III. G can be accepted by a deterministic PDA.

Which combination below expresses all the true statements about G?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: abab can be derived as S S with different splits (and [latex]S\rightarrow\epsilon[/latex] gives more trees) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ambiguous True
- II: G only makes concatenations of "ab" and "ba", so "aabb" (equal counts) is missing False
- III: L(G) = [latex](ab+ba)^*[/latex] is regular, so a DPDA accepts it True

Answer: I and III only

questions.text: Let [latex]L=\left\{w \in(0+1)^{*} \mid w \text { has even number of } 1 \text { 's }\right\}[/latex], i.e. [latex]L[/latex] is the set of all bit strings with even number of 1's. Which one of the regular expression below represents [latex]L[/latex]?
questions.solution:
[latex]0^*(10^*10^*)^*[/latex]: leading 0s, then groups that each contain exactly two 1s (with any 0s around). That gives exactly the strings with an even number of 1s.

- [latex](0^*10^*1)^*[/latex] cannot end with 0 (e.g. "110").
- [latex]0^*(10^*1^*)^*0^*[/latex] allows odd counts (e.g. "1").
- Option 4 forces at least two 1s at fixed places, missing "" and "0".

Answer: [latex]0^*(10^*10^*)^*[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: An FSM(finite state machine) can be considered to be a turing machine of finite tape length
questions.solution:
A finite automaton reads its input once, left to right, and never goes back or writes. That is a TM whose head only moves one way and cannot rewind.

Answer: without rewinding capability and unidirectional tape movement

questions.text: Which one of the following grammars is free from left recursion?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 1: [latex]A\rightarrow Aa[/latex] is directly left recursive.
- Option 2: S, A, B never start with themselves, directly or indirectly True
- Option 3: [latex]S\rightarrow Aa[/latex] and [latex]A\rightarrow Sc[/latex] give [latex]S\Rightarrow Sca[/latex] (indirect).
- Option 4: [latex]A\rightarrow Bd[/latex] and [latex]B\rightarrow Ae[/latex] give [latex]A\Rightarrow Aed[/latex] (indirect).

Answer: Option 2

questions.text:
Consider the following languages.
L1 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex] |M takes at least 2016 steps on some input},
L2 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex]| M takes at least 2016 steps on all inputs} and
L3 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M|M accepts [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]},
where for each Turing machine M, [latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex] denotes a specific encoding of M. Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
In 2016 steps a TM reads at most the first 2016 input symbols, so only inputs of length up to 2016 matter. Simulating M on all of them for 2016 steps decides both L1 and L2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] recursive.

L3 (M accepts [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]) is a non-trivial property of L(M) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable (Rice).

Answer: L1, L2 are recursive and L3 is not recursive
